activity.notes: The Civilization-mod spelling 'Kalonga Mazula' is normalized to the historically attested form Kalonga Muzura. Early seventeenth-century Portuguese records and modern scholarship identify Muzura as Kalonga of the Maravi. He was already a military ally of Gatsi Rusere by 1608, hosted Gaspar Bocarro in 1616, defeated Lundu in 1622, and was still described as a powerful ruler in Portuguese records in 1635. Because the exact accession and death years are uncertain, ATLAS uses a conservative documented ruling-activity window of c.1608–c.1635 rather than inventing a full reign.

sources.title: Long-distance trade and the rise of the Maravi empire — Archaeology and Oral Tradition in Malawi
sources.citation_text: Yusuf M. Juwayeyi's academic study uses early seventeenth-century Portuguese records and identifies Kalonga Muzura among the Maravi rulers involved in regional military and commercial politics.

sources.title: Maravi
sources.citation_text: The compiled chronology, citing Juwayeyi and Kings M. Phiri, records Muzura as Kalonga before/around 1608, active through the 1630s, with death in the 1640s; ATLAS uses only the conservative attested 1608–1635 activity window.
